body.objective: Detect and safely repair divergence between authoritative committed Science Forge deliveries and the shared physical worktree. The new read-only `s-f git status` correctly exposed a distinct failure mode beyond a stale shared index: completed Observer artifacts are present in `origin/master` and local HEAD, but 274 tracked files are physically absent from the shared worktree (approximately 557,382 deleted lines versus `origin/master`). This can break later atlas, paper, certificate and reverse-coverage rebuilds even though provenance in Git is intact. The current safe-actions text offers no scoped materialization operation, while raw restore/reset is forbidden in the concurrent shared tree.
body.stop_condition: First preserve the landed read-only truth surface. Add a typed committed-worktree drift audit that compares a selected authoritative revision (normally the programme integration head or fetched origin/master) with the physical programme-root worktree independently of the shared index, and distinguishes: missing committed path; worktree blob equal to an older base; genuine uncommitted edit; untracked collision; live leased path; and safely materializable committed blob. Attribute affected paths to WORK_COMMITTED/work-report changed-path manifests where possible. Add a coordinator-only scoped materialization command, preferably by work item, delivery commit or explicit manifest, that reads blobs from the named immutable commit and writes only paths proven absent or byte-equal to the declared older base; it must use compare-and-swap preconditions, touch no Git index, refuse every modified/untracked/live-lease collision, and emit an append-only WORKTREE_MATERIALIZED or typed refusal receipt with before/after hashes. Integrate a compact health finding into overview when terminal committed deliverables are physically absent and no live owner is present. Make work commit/submit/integrate verify after sealing that every declared delivery path still has a typed physical disposition; do not silently delete or dematerialize producer files. Add deterministic two-agent regressions for new files, modified files, intentional deletions, concurrent edits, stale local HEAD, fetched-ahead origin, partial materialization, crash/resume and byte-stable refusal. Use the current completed Observer delivery as a large-programme regression: the audit must identify the 274 missing tracked files without classifying Bridge/Classical live edits as safe repairs, and a dry-run must propose only conflict-free Observer paths.
body.forbid: no git reset, checkout, restore, clean, broad read-tree, shared-index replacement or add-all; no overwrite of a modified/untracked path; no materialization across a live lease without holder acknowledgement; no assumption that origin/master is authoritative without a fetched revision and explicit programme policy; no automatic work transition or scientific claim promotion; no deleting historical events; no treating a clean Git commit as proof that the physical worktree is usable; no global serialization of independent agents
body.resource_hint: SCIENCE FORGE GIT/WORKTREE PAPERCUT. Reuse SF16's private-index truth scan and SF9's WORK_COMMITTED manifests. Detection is immediately useful; mutation may land later if the CAS proof is too risky. The current large fixture is read-only reproducible with `git diff --stat origin/master -- physics/symplectic-reconstruction/closed_universe_observers` and selected `git cat-file -e origin/master:<path>` checks.
notes: Live reproduction at 2026-07-21T10:13Z: `s-f git status` reports real deletions under closed_universe_observers while `git cat-file -e origin/master:physics/symplectic-reconstruction/closed_universe_observers/certificates/PHASE1_RELATIONAL_OBSERVABLE_DISPOSITION_SYNTHESIS_V1.json` succeeds and the physical file is absent.
The same scan shows Bridge and Classical have active worktree differences, so a broad restoration is unsafe. The required recovery must be manifest-scoped and fail closed on any collision.

This is distinct from sf:forge-request/science-forge-shared-index-staleness-status-surface: SF16 correctly reports HEAD-to-worktree truth, but does not provide provenance-aware attribution, overview health, or a safe way to rematerialize committed terminal deliveries.
